<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 96:9">Ib. XCVI, 9</cite> <he>רְתוֹתוּ</he> ed. Lag. (ed. Wil. <he>רְתִתוּ</he>).
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 77:17">Ib. LXXVII, 17</cite> <he>רְתִיתוּן</he> ed. Lag. (ed. Wil. <he>רְתַתּוּן</he>); a. fr.—
<cite ref="Bava Batra 167a:7">B. Bath. 167ᵃ</cite> <he>דרְתִיתָא ידיה</he> Rashb. whose hand trembled (ed. <he>דרָתֵית ידיה</he>, Ms. R. <he>דמִירְתַת</he> who trembled with his hand).
Targ. Job IV, 10 מְרַתְּתִין כרכיא וכ׳ Ms. (ed. Lag. מריתיתין, corr. acc., or מַרְתִּיתִין Af.; ed. Wil. a. oth. מרתיהין כרביא, כדביא, corr. acc.) frighten cities with their robberies.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Numbers 21:34">Targ. Y. I Num. XXI, 34</cite>.
<cite ref="Chullin 96a">Ḥull. 96ᵃ</cite> <he>א׳ נפל וכ׳</he> he was frightened, and the knife fell out of his hand.

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 22b:6">Ab. Zar. 22ᵇ</cite> <he>אינהו … מִירְתְּתֵי אנן … לא מִרְתְּתֵי</he> they (the gentiles) who know one another’s ways are afraid (lest they be watched); of us who know not their habits, they are not afraid.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 22b:7">Ib.</cite> <he>מִירְתְּתָא</he> she is afraid. B. Bath. l. c., v. supra.
